source.method: Parsed every WXR <item> with wp:post_type=tablepress_table; matched the 29 canonical category titles by exact string (A1-A4, B1-B16, C1-C9); each match's content:encoded is a JSON array-of-arrays (header row + data rows); every <a href> found in the "Resource Link" column became one output resource row, inheriting that table row's Topic/Name cell (forward-filled from the nearest preceding non-blank Topic cell, same convention already used for Where-Sanskrit/What-Sanskrit) and Description cell (when the table has one — some categories only have 2 columns, no description).

excludedDuplicate.reason: Stray/abandoned duplicate, not referenced by the live page. Its row count (9 resource links) does not match the live-rendered A1 category (35 links); the canonical table (id 11855, 35 links) does match.

totals.nonLinkRowsExplanation: 23 rows carry no link at all, by design, not by extraction error: 4 are the literal "Note - Currently, no links are available..." placeholder text on categories B11/B13/B15/B16 (confirmed empty on the live page itself), and 19 are C8 "Tips and Tricks"' real advice paragraphs, which the live page presents as plain text, never as clickable links.

C 2 - Computational Tools.desc: This tool provides conversion facility among the romanised transliteration schemes into Devanāgarī and also from Devanāgarī into various romanised transliteration schemes. This site also provides tools for analysis of Sanskrit processing: morphological analysis and generation, segmentation, sandhi splitter, and parsing.

C 2 - Computational Tools.title: https://sambhasha.ksu.ac.in
C 2 - Computational Tools.desc: The primary intent of this website is to develop various computational tools for Saṃskṛta and allied languages like - Mahākośa- a kośa data navigation tool. Āyussaṃkṛtam-Courseware for Āyurvedic Medical students. Tarkasaṅgrahaḥ Ontologicalknowledge representation Vāṅmayī-e Create text – explore the meaning. Sāṅgaṇikapāli-Pali language tools Prācīnanyāyaḥ-Ontological knowledge representation Sandhi Splitting tool Bhaṭṭikāvya-nandinī-Explore Bhattikavya with Kāraka dependency diagram Vaijayantīkośa-Knowledge net Nāmadhāturūpikā-Denominative verbs Śabdakautukam-Practice noun forms Anvayacitraṇam-tool Draw relations.

C 2 - Computational Tools.title: https://cfilt.iitb.ac.in
C 2 - Computational Tools.desc: This webpage has been designed to provide a lexical database for Saṃskṛta. It is related to source materials like - Multilingual wordnets and ontologies and their linking, resolving word and attachment ambiguities, identifying correct parts of speech, named entities and non-recursive noun phrases for Marathi and Hindi, Indian language query to English and Hindi Retrieval, automatic translation involving Marathi, Hindi and English, testing if a piece text (hypothesis) is inferable from another (text), detecting polarity-positive/negative/neutral- of a given document, especially reviews, studying cognitive aspects of language processing and understanding using eye-tracking. All these are processed with help of CFILT - Computation for Indian Language Technology that primarily focuses on deep semantics and multilinguality that played a pivotal role in these activities by laying stress on semantics has led to research in the above mentioned areas.

C 2 - Computational Tools.title: https://sanskrit.inria.fr
C 2 - Computational Tools.desc: The Sanskrit Heritage Site provides various services for the computational treatment for Sanskrit like – Dictionary Access (with morphology generator), a rich encyclopedic content about Bhāratīya Culture and other phonological tools like parser and so on.

C 2 - Computational Tools.title: https://www.sanskrit-linguistics.org
C 2 - Computational Tools.desc: This forum is a sandhi-spilt corpus of Saṃskṛta texts with morphological and lexical analysis. It has been designed for text historical research in Saṃskṛta linguistics and philology wherein the users can search for words and their collocations in a corpus of more than 48 lakh manually tagged words in 6 lakh plus text lines.

C 2 - Computational Tools.topic: Centre of Sanskrit Studies, Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU)
C 2 - Computational Tools.title: https://sanskrit.jnu.ac.in
C 2 - Computational Tools.desc: The website hosts a wide range of tools and resources, including online lexical resources such as the Amarakośa, searchable corpora of classical texts like the Mahābhārata, Bhagavad Gītā, Āyurveda texts, Raghuvaṃśa, and selected Upaniṣads, as well as manuscript-related resources. It provides computational linguistics tools such as morphological analyzers, sandhi splitters and generators, subanta and tiṅanta analyzers, POS tagging utilities, and other Pāṇinīyan grammar–based language-processing tools. In addition, the site includes annotated corpora, research datasets, e-learning and multimedia resources, and information on ongoing research projects, workshops, and academic initiatives, making it a key platform for researchers, students, and practitioners working in Saṃskṛta studies, digital humanities, and Indic language computing.

C 2 - Computational Tools.topic: The Sanskrit Library – Tools and Resources
C 2 - Computational Tools.title: https://www.sanskritlibrary.org
C 2 - Computational Tools.desc: This tools page aggregates a wide range of digital resources, including text viewers, parsers, analyzers, dictionaries, corpora, and encoding standards. It supports scholarly research, teaching, and computational analysis of Saṃskṛta through standardized digital formats and open-access tools.

C 2 - Computational Tools.desc: It provides tools for cross-referencing, contextual lookup, and thematic navigation across classical literature. C 2 - Computational Tools.title: https://ihdia.iiit.ac.in/unilipi/
C 2 - Computational Tools.desc: A Unified Multi-Script OCR for Historical Indic Manuscripts. It is a single OCR foundation model trained jointly across 13 Indic scripts. UniLipi currently processes manuscripts written in: Devanagari, Sharada, Modi, Gurmukhi, Jaini, Bengali, Odia, Grantha, Telugu, Malayalam, Kannada, Newar, and Siddham. More scripts in the pipeline. Beyond historical manuscripts, UniLipi also transfers to contemporary Indic handwriting. This project is developed at IIIT Hyderabad as part of LekhyaAI.

C 8 - Tips and Tricks.title: 1. Choose the appropriate script and transliteration Use all 3 input methods – devanāgarī, IAST, and general English to find varied results and choose the best amongst the same.
2. Begin with standard and authoritative websites Start your research using well-established "master" or reference websites before moving to secondary or derivative sources.
3. Use precise and infrequent keywords Prefer specific technical terms and apply selective or advanced search techniques to avoid generic or irrelevant results.
4. Perform iterative searches Refine and repeat your searches by modifying keywords, scripts, and platforms to progressively improve accuracy and depth.

5. Combine multiple repositories for completeness Use a combination of digital libraries and repositories to obtain a comprehensive and reliable picture; prioritize major or "mother" repositories wherever possible.
6. Verify rigorously before concluding Do not finalize findings until they are fully confirmed; when possible, validate references by consulting a Guru or subject-matter scholar.
1. Use the "related:" search operator to find similar websites. Enter related:chinmaya.org in the search bar to discover multiple websites associated with or similar to the Chinmaya network.
2. Select the language and script strategically Choose Sanskrit or English based on the nature of the content you are searching for.
3. Search basic texts (mūlam) in Devanagari For original Sanskrit sources and primary texts, always search using Devanagari script.
4. Search translations and explanations in English or IAST For commentaries, translations, and secondary literature, use English keywords or IAST transliteration.
5. Use advanced search options Click on the "Advanced Search" option to apply filters such as exact phrases, site-specific searches, or file types.
6. Apply time filters to refine results After performing a search, use the "Tools" option to limit results to a specific time period for recent or historical relevance.
7. Combine multiple content types Use a mix of images, videos, news, and text-based results to gain broader context and deeper insight into the topic.
8. Use exact phrases within quotation marks Place keywords inside inverted commas to search for an exact phrase, e.g., "Chinmaya bhagavad-gītā", to obtain precise and relevant results.

9. Use plus, minus, and Boolean operators Force inclusion or exclusion of terms using + and –, or apply Boolean logic such as AND, OR, XOR, and NOT (where supported) to refine searches in academic databases.
10. Search by document type Use file extensions like doc, pdf, or xls, or apply the command filetype:pdf, to locate specific types of documents.
11. Restrict searches to specific websites Combine your search term with site:www.abc.org to find relevant content within a particular website or domain.
12. Use an asterisk (*) for unknown words Insert an asterisk in place of missing or uncertain words; the search engine may automatically fill in the gap and return relevant variations.
